overview.title: Cloning produces a second owning collection
overview.explanation: Ownership arrows identify which collection destroys each object. The dashed clone dependency describes creation and copying; it does not mean that the clone borrows the original. Both ListCue objects own separate vectors of string values. The text cue follows the same ownership shape and is omitted only to keep this view focused.

focus.title: Copy the concrete object behind a base interface
focus.start: // Copy the vector and its strings.
focus.what: The clone copies value-owned members; rename edits only one object’s first string.
focus.where: The ListCue implementation of copying and editing.
focus.why: The concrete class knows how its state should duplicate.
focus.invariant: Every list stays nonempty, every name stays nonempty, and copies remain independent.
focus.risk: Replacing the value vector with shared mutable storage would require a new copy policy.

focus.title: The caller copies without a type switch
focus.start: // No concrete type is named here.
focus.what: This loop duplicates heterogeneous cues through one operation.
focus.where: main, after creating the original owning collection.
focus.why: Type-specific copying stays inside each concrete cue.
focus.invariant: Every new owning handle refers to an independent object with equivalent initial value.
focus.risk: Copying a unique_ptr directly will not compile; wrapping its raw pointer creates double ownership.
explain: The comment identifies the absence of concrete-type decisions.
